mainTopic: The deadlines for the nighttime קריאת שמע and for eating the קרבן פסח: dawn, חצות, and the 'time of haste'
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי שמעון's ברייתא. The time after עמוד השחר is legally day, but it is called 'night' because people are still asleep. רבי יהושע בן לוי was reported to rule like רבי שמעון, and רבי זירא adds that one should not say השכיבנו then. רב יצחק בר יוסף shows that this ruling was only inferred from a story, and it applies only בשעת הדחק. Next, the גמרא explains רבן גמליאל's sons: they were asking whether the חכמים truly disagree with their father. He answers that the חכמים agree the time lasts until dawn, and 'until חצות' is only a fence against sin. The משנה leaves eating the קרבן פסח off its until-dawn list. רב יוסף explains this as a מחלוקת: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says until חצות, and רבי עקיבא says until dawn. The גמרא traces their sources and matches them to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי אבא then explains the argument as one over whose 'haste' the תורה means. Finally, an אגדה begins: הקדוש ברוך הוא asked ישראל, 'please,' to borrow silver and gold from מצרים, and the reason continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The time after dawn is really day, but called night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רבי שמעון's ברייתא. The time after עמוד השחר is day. It is called 'night' only because some people are still sleeping then.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is day. They call it 'night' because there are people who are still asleep at that time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before this text. How can the second ברייתא say both readings are 'in the day', which makes the time before sunrise day, and also count the reading then as the nighttime שמע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer: legally, the time before sunrise (after עמוד השחר) is truly day, which is why the ברייתא says both readings are 'in the day'. The reading then is still called the 'night' reading only because many people are still asleep then. That is also why, if needed, that hour can still count as 'when you lie down' (בשכבך) for someone who missed the nighttime שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (used to say: the simple reading is correct after all)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the time after dawn is legally night. It is legally day. The word 'night' here is only a description of what people are doing at that hour.

phrases.english: No, it really is day,
phrases.notes: He means the time right after עמוד השחר, which the ברייתא had called 'night.'

phrases.english: and the fact that they call it "night"
is because there are people who sleep at that time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the self-contradiction raised just before this text on רבי שמעון's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading a term: 'night' is descriptive language, not the legal category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls the time before sunrise 'day' (both readings are 'in the day'), yet treats a reading then as the nighttime שמע, which seems contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is legally day. It is called 'night' only because people are still asleep then.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר רבי חנינא reports in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון's ruling in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אחא בר רבי חנינא said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי: the הלכה is like רבי שמעון, who said it in the name of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the ברייתא makes sense, the גמרא brings a practical ruling. We follow רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's position is that someone can read the nighttime שמע after עמוד השחר, before sunrise. This statement makes that position the practical הלכה. Later steps will question how strongly רבי יהושע בן לוי actually held it.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the claim that רב יצחק בר יוסף will soon correct, so remember exactly what was reported here.

phrases.english: Rabbi Aḥa son of Rabbi Ḥanina said,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The halacha is like Rabbi Shimon
who said it in the name of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן שֶׁאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the ברייתא, gives the practical ruling on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון: the nighttime שמע may be read after עמוד השחר, before sunrise.

steps.title: Do not say השכיבנו at that time
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא adds a condition. Someone reading the nighttime שמע after dawn should not say the ברכה of השכיבנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: as long as he does not say 'השכיבנו' (help us lie down).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא puts a limit on the ruling just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may read the nighttime שמע at that hour, but the ברכה of השכיבנו asks for a peaceful night's sleep. That does not fit when it is already day. So the שמע itself is allowed, but this ברכה is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The evening ברכה 'Help us lie down' in peace

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
As long as he does not say "Hashkivenu."
phrases.notes: השכיבנו is the ברכה after the evening שמע, asking God to let us lie down in peace.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When reading the nighttime שמע after dawn, one does not say השכיבנו.

steps.title: The ruling was only inferred, not said outright
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף arrives and reports that רבי יהושע בן לוי never stated this הלכה explicitly. It was only inferred from something he said.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: what רבי אחא בר רבי חנינא reported from רבי יהושע בן לוי was not said outright. It was learned by inference.
steps.whatsHappening: A new report challenges how the ruling in step 2 was passed along. This step is setting up the story that explains where the inference came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 sounded like a clear, general ruling. Now we learn that רבי יהושע בן לוי never actually said 'the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.' People drew that conclusion from a specific incident. That could make the ruling much narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to Bavel)
By inference, drawn out from something else

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אֲמַר:
phrases.english: When Rav Yitzḥak bar Yosef came, he said:
This that Rabbi Aḥa son of Rabbi Ḥanina
said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
was not said explicitly,
rather, it was said by inference.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Corrects the way the ruling in step 2 was reported.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects that רבי יהושע בן לוי issued an explicit, general ruling. It does not reject that he valued רבי שמעון's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling was reported as explicit when it was really only an inference from an incident.

steps.title: The wedding story: rely on רבי שמעון only under pressure
steps.stepSummary: Two רבנן got drunk at the wedding of רבי יהושע בן לוי's son and missed the nighttime שמע. He told them רבי שמעון is worthy to rely on בשעת הדחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pair of רבנן got drunk at the wedding feast of רבי יהושע בן לוי's son. They came before רבי יהושע בן לוי, and he said: רבי שמעון is worthy to rely on in a pressing situation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story that the inference came from. It shows what רבי יהושע בן לוי really said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He did not say 'the הלכה is like רבי שמעון.' He said you may lean on רבי שמעון when you are in a bind. So reading the nighttime שמע after dawn is only an emergency allowance, not something to plan on.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע בן לוי did not rule outright like רבי שמעון. Reading the nighttime שמע after עמוד השחר is allowed only בשעת הדחק, when you truly missed it, and even then without השכיבנו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how much the wording of a ruling matters. 'The הלכה is like him' and 'you may rely on him under pressure' lead to very different practical results.

phrases.english: For there was a certain pair of Sages
who got drunk at the wedding celebration
of the son of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי,
phrases.english: They came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
phrases.notes: The text leaves it unsaid, but they had slept past dawn and were asking if they could still read the nighttime שמע.

phrases.english: he said: Rabbi Shimon is worthy
to rely upon in a pressing situation.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדַאי הוּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִסְמוֹךְ עָלָיו בִּשְׁעַת הַדְּחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the incident from which the ruling was inferred, as step 4 claimed.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע בן לוי's view was only inferred, and only for pressing situations.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the two drunk רבנן at his son's wedding and his reply to them.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון may be relied on only בשעת הדחק, not as a general הלכה.

steps.title: Quoting the story of רבן גמליאל's sons
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the story in the משנה about רבן גמליאל's sons.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'It happened that his sons came...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן גמליאל's sons came home from a wedding feast after midnight and asked if they could still read שמע. He told them that if dawn has not yet come, they must read. The גמרא now zooms in on this story.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual event or story, often brought to show the הלכה in practice
'Etc.'; the rest of the quoted line is assumed

phrases.english: The incident where his sons came, etc.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's story: רבן גמליאל's sons came home from a wedding feast after midnight and asked about reading שמע.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of רבי שמעון and returns to the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the story of the sons for analysis.

steps.title: Didn't the sons already know their father's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the sons had to ask at all, since they surely knew רבן גמליאל holds that שמע may be read until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until now they had not heard this ruling of רבן גמליאל?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that the sons asked their father. They lived with him and must have known his view that שמע can be read all night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's opinion in the משנה is that the time for the nighttime שמע lasts until dawn. His own sons should know that. So their question seems pointless, and the גמרא wants to know what they were really asking.

phrases.english: And until now they had not heard
this ruling of Rabban Gamliel?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sons' question to their father in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sons surely knew their father's opinion, so why would they ask?

steps.title: The sons were asking whether the חכמים argue with their father
steps.stepSummary: The sons knew their father's view. They wanted to know whether the חכמים truly disagree, which would make the הלכה follow the majority, or whether the חכמים agree and 'until חצות' is only a fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what they were saying to him: Do the חכמים disagree with you? If so, when one argues against many, the הלכה follows the many. Or maybe the חכמים agree with you, and when they say 'until midnight' it is only to keep a person away from sin?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the sons were not asking what their father thinks. They were asking whether the חכמים really disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים truly disagree, then רבן גמליאל is one against many, and the הלכה would follow the חכמים, so the sons could not read after midnight. If the חכמים really agree and only set midnight as a protective fence, then after the fact one may still read until dawn. That is the real question.

keyTerms.meaning: When one argues against many, the הלכה follows the many
To keep a person far from sin, a protective fence

steps.confusionAlert: The sons were not asking 'What is your opinion?' They were asking 'What is the חכמים' opinion?' Their father's view only decides the הלכה if the חכמים do not truly argue with him.

phrases.english: This is what they were saying to him:
Do the Rabbis disagree with you?
And with an individual against many, the halakha follows the many.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא רַבָּנַן כְּווֹתָךְ סְבִירָא לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Or perhaps the Rabbis hold like you,
and when they say 'until midnight'
it is in order to keep a person far from sin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by redefining what the sons were asking.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sons seemed to be asking their father's own opinion, which they should have known.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were asking whether the חכמים truly disagree with him or only made a protective fence.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל: the חכמים agree with me, so you must still read
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל answers that the חכמים agree the time lasts until dawn. 'Until חצות' is only a fence, so his sons are still obligated to read שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: The חכמים hold like me, and you are obligated. When they say 'until midnight,' it is only to keep a person far from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל answers his sons: there is no real argument. The חכמים agree with him, so the sons must read שמע now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the חכמים agree that the real time lasts until dawn, there is no case of 'one against many.' The midnight limit is only a protective fence, so after the fact the obligation still applies. That is why he tells them 'you are obligated.'
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, even the חכמים agree the nighttime שמע can be read until dawn. Their 'until חצות' is a fence to stop people from pushing it off too late.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that 'until חצות' in the משנה is a rabbinic fence, not the true end of the time. So someone who is late is still obligated to read.

phrases.english: He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנָן כְּווֹתִי סְבִירָא לְהוּ, וְחַיָּיבִין אַתֶּם.
phrases.english: The Rabbis hold like me, and you are obligated.
And when they say 'until midnight'
it is in order to keep a person far from sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: רַבָּנָן כְּווֹתִי סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבן גמליאל's answer to the sons' real question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים agree with רבן גמליאל, and 'until חצות' is only a fence, so the sons must read.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The nighttime שמע may be read until dawn after the fact; midnight is a protective fence.

steps.title: Quoting the next line: 'And not only this did they say'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, where רבן גמליאל says the same rule applies to every place the חכמים said 'until midnight.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not only this did they say, but...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the next line of the משנה to begin a new discussion. This is a setup line for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן גמליאל adds that wherever the חכמים said 'until midnight,' the real time lasts until dawn. The גמרא is about to discuss that broader rule.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זוֹ בִּלְבַד אָמְרוּ, אֶלָּא וְכוּ׳:
phrases.english: And not only this did they say, but rather, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: wherever the חכמים said 'until midnight,' the מצוה can really be done until dawn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the sons' story to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces רבן גמליאל's broader rule that every 'until midnight' really lasts until dawn.

steps.title: Does רבן גמליאל really hold 'until midnight'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן גמליאל says 'not only this did they say.' The phrase sounds like he accepts the 'until חצות' limit, but he holds the time lasts until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבן גמליאל say 'until midnight,' that he teaches 'and not only this did they say'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the wording of רבן גמליאל's line in the משנה, which was quoted in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ולא זו בלבד אמרו' sound as if רבן גמליאל is adding more cases to a 'until חצות' rule that he accepts. But in the משנה he holds that שמע may be read until dawn. So why would he speak as if 'until חצות' were his own rule?

keyTerms.meaning: Does he say? (a challenge: surely he does not)
And not only this did they say

phrases.english: And does Rabban Gamliel say 'until midnight,'
that he teaches 'and not only this did they say'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה line quoted in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's phrase 'ולא זו בלבד אמרו' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase suggests he accepts an 'until חצות' rule, but he holds the time lasts until dawn.

steps.title: He was explaining the view of the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל meant that even the חכמים, who say 'until חצות,' agree the real מצוה lasts until dawn. 'Until חצות' is only a fence.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבן גמליאל said to his sons: Even according to the חכמים, who say 'until midnight,' the מצוה lasts until dawn comes up. When they say 'until midnight,' it is to keep a person far from sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבן גמליאל was not giving his own view. He was explaining what the חכמים really mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ולא זו בלבד אמרו' describes how the חכמים speak. In many places they say 'until חצות' even though the real time is until dawn. So רבן גמליאל is not adopting the limit himself. He is showing that the חכמים set it only as a protective fence.

keyTerms.meaning: To keep a person far from sin (a fence)

steps.whatToRemember: Whenever the חכמים say 'until חצות,' the real time is until dawn. חצות is only a fence to keep people from sin.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים hold that the מצוה actually ends at חצות. They agree it lasts until dawn. They only set an earlier deadline as a safeguard.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִבְנֵיהּ:
phrases.english: This is what Rabban Gamliel said to his sons:
Even according to the Rabbis, who say 'until midnight,'
its מצוה lasts until dawn comes up.
And the fact that they say 'until midnight'
is in order to keep a person far from sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לְהוּ רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לִבְנֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 11 by explaining what רבן גמליאל meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל seemed to be accepting 'until חצות' as his own rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was explaining that the חכמים also hold the time lasts until dawn. 'Until חצות' is only a fence against sin.

steps.title: Quoting the burning of fats from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: burning the fats and limbs on the מזבח, which may be done until dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: The burning of fats, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, the list of מצוות that last until dawn. This sets up its next comment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists cases where the time lasts until dawn. The first is burning the fats and limbs of קרבנות on the מזבח. By quoting this list, the גמרא prepares to look at what is included in it and what is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the fats (of קרבנות) on the מזבח

phrases.english: The burning of fats, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after finishing the discussion of 'ולא זו בלבד אמרו'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning fats and limbs on the מזבח may be done until dawn.

steps.title: Eating the קרבן פסח is missing from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה's list of 'until dawn' מצוות does not include eating the קרבן פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the eating of the פסח offerings is not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes an observation about the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares the next move, where this will be compared with another source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since eating the פסח is not on the list, it seems its time does not last until dawn. Instead it may follow the 'until חצות' rule. This point will soon be tested against other teachings.

phrases.english: Whereas the eating of the Paschal offerings is not taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from what is missing in the list quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's list of מצוות that last until dawn leaves out eating the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the פסח may be eaten until dawn
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists eating the פסח among the 'until dawn' מצוות. This contradicts the משנה, which left it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: the evening קריאת שמע, הלל on פסח nights, and eating the פסח may all be done until dawn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that clashes with what we just learned from the משנה. The ברייתא says eating the פסח lasts until dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the משנה's silence (Step 14), it sounded like the פסח must be eaten by חצות. This ברייתא puts the פסח right next to קריאת שמע, which lasts until dawn. So the two sources seem to disagree about the deadline for eating the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they threw them together': the גמרא is setting one source against another to show a contradiction
Dawn, the first light of morning
Saying הלל on the night of פסח, together with eating the קרבן

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
The evening recitation of Shema,
and Hallel on the nights of Passover,
and eating the Paschal lamb,
their מצוה lasts until dawn rises!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion drawn in Step 14 from the משנה's omission of the פסח.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference from the משנה that the פסח may only be eaten until חצות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly includes eating the פסח among the מצוות that last until dawn.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the two sources follow two different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that the משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is not a problem. This source follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and that source follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the contradiction. The two sources do not need to agree, because each one follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, which leaves the פסח off its 'until dawn' list, follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says the פסח may only be eaten until חצות. The ברייתא, which allows eating until dawn, follows רבי עקיבא. Next, the גמרא will show where these two opinions come from.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult': the standard opening of an answer
'This one ... that one': matches each source to its own opinion

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: This is not difficult:
this follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
phrases.notes: 'This' means our משנה, which left the פסח off the until-dawn list.

phrases.english: that follows Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: 'That' means the ברייתא from Step 15.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to two different תנאים who disagree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and the ברייתא give one rule and contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They reflect a real disagreement: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says until חצות, and רבי עקיבא says until dawn.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns 'until חצות' from 'this night'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה compares 'this night' of eating the פסח to 'this night' of מכת בכורות, which happened at midnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: Here it says 'this night,' and later it says 'I will pass through Egypt on this night.' Just as there it means until midnight, here too it means until midnight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove there really is a מחלוקת, as רב יוסף said. First we hear רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words 'this night' appear for eating the פסח and for מכת בכורות. מכת בכורות happened at midnight. So רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses this link to say that eating the פסח also ends at midnight.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It says here ... and it says there': the setup for learning one פסוק from another through shared words
'Just as there ... so too here': carries the rule from one פסוק over to the other

phrases.english: As it was taught:
'And they shall eat the meat on this night,'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:8

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
It says here 'on this night,'
and it says further on:
'And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night,'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:12. This is about מכת בכורות.

phrases.english: just as there it was until midnight,
phrases.notes: מכת בכורות came at midnight, as the תורה says elsewhere.

phrases.english: so too here it is until midnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב יוסף's answer by showing the source of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
steps.raayaObject: That a תנא holds the פסח may be eaten only until חצות, as the משנה implies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא linking 'this night' in שמות 12:8 to 'this night' in שמות 12:12.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the פסח is eaten until the 'time of haste'
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא pushes back. The תורה says to eat the פסח 'in haste,' which means until the time of the rush to leave Egypt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Doesn't it already say 'in haste'? That means until the time of haste.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers רבי אלעזר בן עזריה with a different פסוק. He holds the deadline is the 'time of haste,' not midnight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rush to leave Egypt happened in the morning. So 'until the time of haste' means the פסח may be eaten until dawn. That is the view of the ברייתא in Step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But was it not already said?': pointing to a פסוק that seems to settle the question
'In haste': how the תורה says to eat the פסח
The time of the rush, when בני ישראל hurried out of Egypt

steps.confusionAlert: 'The time of haste' is not midnight. Even though מכת בכורות came at midnight, the actual rush out of Egypt was in the morning. That is why רבי עקיבא's view gives until dawn.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
But was it not already said 'in haste'?
phrases.notes: שמות 12:11

phrases.english: Until the time of haste.
phrases.notes: The rush to leave Egypt was in the morning, so this means until dawn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's derivation in Step 17 using a different פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's ruling that the פסח may only be eaten until חצות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק 'in haste' sets the deadline at the time of leaving Egypt, which was in the morning.

steps.title: Then why does the תורה say 'at night'?
steps.stepSummary: If 'in haste' already sets the deadline, the word 'at night' seems to have no job. The ברייתא asks what it teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'at night'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא, still speaking in the ברייתא, raises a question on his own approach: what is the word 'at night' for? This sets up the next step, which explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not use 'this night' to set a deadline, so the word seems extra. Every word in the תורה must teach something. So we need to find a new job for 'at night.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'If so': following through on the view just stated
'What does the verse come to teach?': asking why a word was needed

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'at night'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word 'at night' teaches according to רבי עקיבא's view in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'at night' teaches, if it does not set the midnight deadline.

steps.title: 'At night' teaches that the פסח is eaten at night, not by day
steps.stepSummary: Without 'at night,' we might think the פסח is eaten by day like other קרבנות. The word teaches that it is eaten only at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought it is eaten by day, like other קדשים. So the verse says 'at night': at night it is eaten, and not by day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from Step 19. According to רבי עקיבא, 'at night' tells us when the פסח is eaten. It does not set a deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other קרבנות are normally eaten by day, so we might have treated the פסח the same way. 'At night' teaches that the פסח is different, because it is a nighttime meal. So for רבי עקיבא, 'in haste' gives the deadline of dawn, and 'at night' gives the time of eating.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought': introduces a wrong idea that the פסוק comes to rule out

steps.whatToRemember: There is a מחלוקת about the deadline for eating the קרבן פסח. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says until חצות, learned from 'this night' by comparing it to מכת בכורות, and our משנה follows him. רבי עקיבא says until dawn, learned from 'in haste,' and the ברייתא follows him. For רבי עקיבא, 'at night' only teaches that the פסח is eaten at night and not by day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the contradiction from Step 15. The משנה and the ברייתא do not clash; they simply follow two different תנאים.

phrases.english: One might have thought it is eaten by day, like other sacrifices;
therefore the verse says 'at night':
at night it is eaten, and not by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'At night' teaches that the פסח, unlike other קרבנות, is eaten at night and not by day.

steps.title: What does the word 'this' teach according to רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה needs the word 'הזה' for his גזירה שוה. The גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא, who does not use that גזירה שוה, does with the word.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who uses a גזירה שוה, that the תורה had to write 'this.' But for רבי עקיבא, what does he do with this word 'this'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks closely at one word, 'הזה' ('this'), in 'בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה.' It asks what that word is for according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the word 'הזה' builds the link to 'this night' of מכת בכורות, which is how he gets the midnight deadline. רבי עקיבא gets his deadline from 'in haste' instead, so the word 'הזה' seems to have no job for him. The גמרא asks what it teaches him.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (this side is fine, but...)
A link between two פסוקים that share the same word
What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
who holds of a verbal analogy;
phrases.notes: This is the link from step 17 between 'this night' of eating the פסח and 'this night' of מכת בכורות.

phrases.english: it was necessary to write 'this' for him.
But according to Rabbi Akiva,
what does he do with this word 'this'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 20 explained the word 'at night' for רבי עקיבא. Now the גמרא asks about the next word, 'this.'
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word 'הזה' teach according to רבי עקיבא, who does not learn the גזירה שוה from it?

steps.title: 'This night' rules out a second night of eating
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא, 'הזה' teaches that the פסח is eaten only on this one night. Without it, we might have compared the פסח to שלמים and allowed two nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude another night. You might have thought this: the פסח is קדשים קלים and שלמים are also קדשים קלים. שלמים are eaten for two days and one night, so the פסח should be eaten for two nights in place of the two days. That would mean two nights and one day. So the תורה teaches us 'on this night.' On this night it is eaten, and it is not eaten on another night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. For רבי עקיבא, the word 'this' teaches that the פסח may not be eaten on a second night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסח and שלמים belong to the same group, קדשים קלים. So we might have given the פסח the same time limit as a שלמים: two units of eating time with one unit in between. Since the פסח is a nighttime קרבן, that would come out as two nights with a day between them. The word 'הזה' blocks that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought to say
Peace offerings, eaten for two days and the night between

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the פסח stops being קדשים קלים here. It is still in that group. The word 'הזה' only sets a different time limit for eating it.

phrases.english: It comes to exclude another night,
since it would have entered your mind to say:
Since the Paschal lamb is an offering of lesser holiness,
and peace offerings are offerings of lesser holiness,

phrases.aramaic: מָה שְׁלָמִים נֶאֱכָלִין לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד —
phrases.english: just as peace offerings are eaten for two days and one night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף פֶּסַח נֶאֱכָל שְׁתֵּי לֵילוֹת בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנֵי יָמִים,
phrases.english: so too the Paschal lamb is eaten two nights in place of two days,

phrases.aramaic: וִיהֵא נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי לֵילוֹת וְיוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and it would be eaten for two nights and one day.
So it teaches us 'on this night':
on this night it is eaten,
and it is not eaten on another night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 21's question about what 'הזה' teaches for רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הזה' teaches that the פסח is eaten on one night only. It is not like a שלמים, which could have led us to allow two nights and the day between them.

steps.title: Where does רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learn the one-night rule?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses 'הזה' for his גזירה שוה. So the גמרא asks how he knows the פסח is not eaten on a second night.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other side. It asks how רבי אלעזר בן עזריה knows the פסח is not eaten for two nights, since he already used the word 'הזה' for something else. This short line sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every opinion has to keep the rule that the פסח is eaten on only one night. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה already used 'הזה' for the link to מכת בכורות. So he must have another source for this rule.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: where does he learn that there is no second night, if 'this' is already used up?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 22 gave רבי עקיבא's source for the one-night rule. Now the גמרא asks for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's source that the פסח is not eaten on a second night?

steps.title: He learns it from 'do not leave any over until morning'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns the one-night rule from the פסוק 'לא תותירו עד בקר' ('do not leave any of it over until morning').
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'You shall not leave any of it over until morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gets the rule from a different פסוק. That פסוק forbids leaving any of the פסח over until morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you may not leave the meat until the morning, you certainly may not keep eating it the next night. So 'לא תותירו עד בקר' already teaches that there is no second night. That leaves 'הזה' free for his גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out (he learns it) from

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree the פסח is eaten on one night only. רבי עקיבא learns it from 'הזה.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns it from 'לא תותירו עד בקר,' because he uses 'הזה' for the גזירה שוה with מכת בכורות.

phrases.english: He derives it from 'You shall not leave any over until morning.'
phrases.notes: שמות 12:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 23's question by giving רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's separate source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ban on leaving any of the פסח over until morning already rules out eating it on a second night.

steps.title: Why רבי עקיבא cannot rely on 'until morning' alone
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא needs 'הזה' because 'until morning' by itself might mean the second morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does רבי עקיבא need the word 'הזה'? If I only had the פסוק 'do not leave it until morning,' I would have said: which morning? The second morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to רבי עקיבא. It explains why he cannot learn the one-night rule from 'לא תותירו עד בקר' the way רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learned the one-night rule from 'do not leave it until morning.' רבי עקיבא says that פסוק is unclear, because 'morning' could mean the morning after a second night. So he needs 'הזה' ('this night') to make the one-night limit clear.

keyTerms.meaning: If [I learned it only] from there
I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva [why does he need 'this']?
If [I learned it only] from there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the פסוק 'לא תותירו עד בקר' from step 24.

phrases.english: I would have said:
What does 'morning' mean? The second morning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אִי מֵהָתָם הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי עקיבא does not accept the source given for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Until morning' alone could mean the second morning, so רבי עקיבא needs 'הזה' to limit the eating to one night.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: 'morning' always means the first morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rejects the worry and says any plain 'morning' means the next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר would tell you: every 'morning' means the first morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reply to רבי עקיבא's worry. He says the worry is not real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds that when the תורה says 'morning' without saying which one, it always means the very next morning. So 'לא תותירו עד בקר' is already enough to teach one night, and 'הזה' is free for his גזירה שוה.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree the פסח is eaten for only one night. They argue only about which word in the פסוק teaches it, because 'הזה' is needed by רבי אלעזר בן עזריה for his גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar would say to you:
phrases.notes: This is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from the earlier steps, called here by his short name.

phrases.english: Every 'morning' is the first morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי עקיבא's concern from step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that 'בקר' could mean the second morning.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A plain 'morning' in the תורה always means the very next morning, so there is nothing unclear to worry about.

steps.title: The same argument appears in an earlier ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this מחלוקת matches another מחלוקת of תנאים, and quotes the פסוק they argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים. As a ברייתא teaches: 'There you shall slaughter the פסח in the evening, when the sun sets, at the time you left מצרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It announces that another pair of תנאים argue about the same issue, and quotes the פסוק they are explaining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions three times: evening, sunset, and the time of leaving מצרים (which was in the morning). The next two steps show two ways to match these times to the steps of the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: These תנאים argue the same way as those תנאים

phrases.english: And these Tannaim are like those Tannaim.
phrases.notes: 'These' are רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה; 'those' are the two תנאים in the ברייתא that comes next.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"There you shall slaughter the Pesach
phrases.notes: דברים 16:6

phrases.english: in the evening, when the sun sets,
at the time you left Egypt."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides have been explained, the גמרא connects their מחלוקת to an earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת of רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה matches a מחלוקת in a ברייתא about דברים 16:6.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: by the time of leaving מצרים, the פסח is already leftover to burn
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר matches each of the three times to a different stage: slaughtering, eating, and burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: 'In the evening' you slaughter, 'when the sun sets' you eat, and 'at the time you left מצרים' you burn.
steps.whatsHappening: The first תנא in the ברייתא gives his reading of the פסוק. He gives each time in the פסוק its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, by the morning time of leaving מצרים the meat is already leftover (נותר) that must be burned. So the eating must end before morning, like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who says until midnight.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of a קרבן left past its time, which must be burned

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אליעזר (in this ברייתא) with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (in the earlier steps). They are two different תנאים, though רבי אליעזר's view matches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
'In the evening' you slaughter,
phrases.notes: 'Evening' here means the afternoon, before sunset.

phrases.english: and 'when the sun sets' you eat,
and 'at the time you left Egypt' you burn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר בָּעֶרֶב אַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first opinion in the ברייתא quoted in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughter in the afternoon, eat from sunset, and by morning the meat is leftover to be burned. This matches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: you may keep eating until the time of leaving מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the eating continues all the way until the morning time of leaving מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: 'In the evening' you slaughter, 'when the sun sets' you eat. And until when do you keep eating? Until 'the time you left מצרים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second תנא in the ברייתא gives his reading. He treats the time of leaving מצרים as the end of the eating time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, the eating does not end at midnight. It continues until morning, the time of leaving מצרים. This matches רבי עקיבא, which completes the parallel the גמרא announced in step 27.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר matches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (eating ends before morning, at midnight). רבי יהושע matches רבי עקיבא (eating continues until morning).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
'In the evening' you slaughter,
'when the sun sets' you eat,
and until when do you keep on eating?
Until 'the time you left Egypt.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר בָּעֶרֶב אַתָּה זוֹבֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion in the ברייתא, which argues with רבי אליעזר in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח may be eaten from sunset until the morning time of leaving מצרים. This matches רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Everyone agrees: redeemed at night, left by day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says all agree that the גאולה happened at night, but the actual leaving from מצרים happened during the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: Everyone agrees that Israel was redeemed from מצרים only at night, because the פסוק says 'ה׳ took you out of Egypt at night.' And when they actually left, they left only by day, because the פסוק says 'On the day after the פסח, the children of Israel went out with a high hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא starts a new way of explaining the argument between רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא. First he lays out the facts that both sides agree on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two פסוקים seem to clash: one says 'at night' and one says 'by day.' רבי אבא solves this by splitting the event into two parts. The permission to leave (גאולה) came at night, and the physical leaving (יציאה) happened by day.

keyTerms.meaning: They were redeemed (given permission to go free)
With a high hand, openly and proudly
On the day after the פסח

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up 'redeemed' and 'left.' Here they are two different moments: redeemed at night, left in the daytime.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Everyone agrees that when Israel was redeemed from Egypt,
they were redeemed only in the evening,
as it is said: "ה׳ your God took you out of Egypt at night,"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:1

phrases.english: and when they actually left, they left only by day,
as it is said: "On the day after the Pesach
the children of Israel went out with a high hand."
phrases.notes: במדבר 33:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new explanation of the רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and רבי עקיבא מחלוקת. Here both sides argue over the meaning of 'חפזון,' instead of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's גזירה שוה from 'this night'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree that the גאולה happened at night and the leaving happened by day.

steps.title: The argument is about 'haste': רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the Egyptians' haste
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא says the real argument is about the meaning of 'חפזון'. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says it means the Egyptians' rush.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what do they argue about? About the time of 'haste.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds: What is 'haste'? The haste of the Egyptians.
steps.whatsHappening: After showing what both sides agree on, רבי אבא now names the one point they argue about: the word 'חפזון' in the פסוק about eating the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says the פסח must be eaten 'in haste,' so the eating time ends at the moment of haste. If the haste is the Egyptians rushing Israel out after מכת בכורות, that was at midnight. That is why רבי אלעזר בן עזריה limits the eating to midnight.

phrases.english: So about what do they argue?
About the time of "haste,"
phrases.notes: From שמות 12:11: 'you shall eat it in haste.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya holds:
What is "haste"? The haste of the Egyptians.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ — עַל שְׁעַת חִפָּזוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After stating what both agree on, it identifies the real point of argument and gives the first side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, 'חפזון' is the Egyptians' haste at midnight, so the פסח may be eaten until midnight.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא says the haste was Israel's
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that 'חפזון' means Israel's rush to leave, which happened in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא holds: What is 'haste'? The haste of Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the argument: רבי עקיבא's reading of the word 'חפזון.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the haste is Israel hurrying out of מצרים, that happened in the morning. So the time for eating the פסח lasts until morning. This is the same 'בחפזון' reading רבי עקיבא used in step 18. What is new in רבי אבא's version is that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה also reads 'חפזון,' so there is no גזירה שוה from 'this night' here, only an argument over whose haste it means.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אבא, both sides agree on the facts of the night and the day. They argue only about whose haste the תורה means: the Egyptians' (midnight) or Israel's (morning).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva holds:
What is "haste"? The haste of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the argument that was set up in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, 'חפזון' is Israel's haste in the morning, so the פסח may be eaten until morning.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports that the redemption began at night
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how the תורה can say they left 'at night' when they left by day, and answers that the גאולה began in the evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא‎: 'ה׳ your God took you out of Egypt at night.' Did they really leave at night? They left only by day, as it says, 'On the day after the פסח the children of Israel went out with a high hand'! Rather, this teaches that the גאולה began for them in the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבי אבא. It supports his idea that the night and day פסוקים describe two different stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises the same clash between the 'night' פסוק and the 'day' פסוק. It solves it the way רבי אבא did: the leaving was by day, but the גאולה started the night before. This backs up the first part of רבי אבא's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (in a ברייתא)
Is it really so? (opens a surprised question)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי אבא's split between 'redeemed' and 'left' is not his own new idea. It already appears in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
"ה׳ your God took you out of Egypt at night":
Did they really leave at night?
But they left only by day,
as it is said: "On the day after the Pesach
the children of Israel went out with a high hand"!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִתְחִילָה לָהֶם גְּאוּלָּה מִבָּעֶרֶב.
phrases.english: Rather, this teaches that the redemption began for them in the evening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for the first part of רבי אבא's statement (step 30).
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבא's claim that the גאולה happened at night while the leaving happened by day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that answers the clash between 'לילה' (דברים 16:1) and 'ממחרת הפסח' (במדבר 33:3) by saying the גאולה began in the evening.

steps.title: The word 'נא' means 'please'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'דבר נא באזני העם.' The school of רבי ינאי says that 'נא' is always a word of request.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'Speak, please, in the ears of the people.' The school of רבי ינאי said that 'נא' always means 'please.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new אגדה connected to יציאת מצרים. It starts with a פסוק and a short rule about the word 'נא.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new topic grows out of the earlier discussion about leaving מצרים. The school of רבי ינאי teaches that 'נא' is not an extra word; it shows that someone is asking politely. This sets up the question of why הקדוש ברוך הוא would need to ask politely.

keyTerms.meaning: Please; a word used when making a request
A way of speaking that makes a request
The school, or students, of רבי ינאי
And so on; the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: "Speak, please, in the ears of the people," etc.
phrases.notes: שמות 11:2

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
"Na" is nothing other than an expression of request.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אֵין ״נָא״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן בַּקָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new אגדה on the topic of יציאת מצרים, which the previous steps were discussing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'נא' in a פסוק always means a request, 'please.'

steps.title: God pleads with משה to have Israel borrow silver and gold
steps.stepSummary: הקדוש ברוך הוא asks משה, 'please,' to ask ישראל, 'please,' to borrow silver and gold vessels from מצרים. He begins to give the reason, 'so that he should not say.'
steps.simpleTranslation: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to משה: I ask you, please go and tell ישראל: I ask you, please borrow silver and gold vessels from the Egyptians, so that he should not say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the polite request was. It also starts to give the reason, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of 'please' here. הקדוש ברוך הוא asks משה, and משה asks ישראל. The words 'שלא יאמר' prepare us for the reason behind this polite request, which continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: I ask of you, please (speaking to one person)
I ask of you, please (speaking to many people)
So that he should not say

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. 'So that he should not say' leads into the reason that the גמרא gives next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:
Please, I ask of you,
go and say to them, to Israel:
Please, I ask of you all,
borrow from Egypt
vessels of silver and vessels of gold,
so that he should not say

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה: בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule that 'נא' means 'please' and spells out the request הקדוש ברוך הוא made.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הקדוש ברוך הוא pleaded with משה, and through him with ישראל, to borrow silver and gold from the Egyptians. The reason begins with 'so that he should not say.'
